## Questions and answers
### What is a B-lender?
A federally or provincially regulated lender — like a trust company or credit union — that takes on files banks decline. Rates are higher, but the path to ownership is real.

### How are B-lender rates different?
Typically 1–3% higher than A-lender rates, plus a lender fee. I'm transparent about this upfront — there are no surprises on closing day.

### Will applying hurt my credit score?
A single mortgage application is one hard inquiry — minimal impact. I do a soft pull first before we go anywhere near a formal application.

### How long until I can refinance to A-lender rates?
Usually 12–24 months of on-time payments and a recovering credit profile is enough. I track this with you and tell you when you're ready.

### What documents do I need?
Depends on your situation — but typically ID, 3–6 months of bank statements, proof of income (T4, NOA, or business financials), and a property address. I'll give you a specific list on our first call.

### What are your fees?
I'm paid by the lender on most deals. On some private/B files there's a broker fee — I'll tell you the exact number before you commit to anything.

### What is a private mortgage?
A short-term loan, usually one to two years, from a private lender or mortgage investment company. It's approved mainly on your property's equity rather than your income or credit. It costs more than a B-lender, so I use it as a bridge: solve the problem now, then move you to a better rate.
